dedupe_keys.name: noaa gnome desktop oil spill trajectory model general noaa operational modeling environment

description: Desktop GNOME, the General NOAA Operational Modeling Environment, is the oil spill trajectory model that NOAA's Office of Response and Restoration used to predict the route a pollutant might follow in or on a body of water. Users describe a spill scenario and GNOME produces an oil spill movie of the predicted trajectory, with estimates of oil beached, still floating or evaporated at given times, how wind, currents and other processes move and spread the oil, the effect of uncertainty in current and wind forecasts, and physical and chemical weathering. Standard Mode uses regional Location Files that package tide and current data, such as for Prince William Sound or Long Island Sound; Diagnostic Mode lets responders incorporate outside circulation models. The latest desktop version is 1.3.10 of November 2017, and NOAA states the desktop version has been replaced by the web-based WebGNOME, is not maintained and was last updated in September 2019. Access: Windows and Mac downloads, manual, location files and ArcGIS toolkits from the page, free. Caveats: unmaintained software with unspecified licence. It suits emergency response and exposure studies of marine oil spills from tankers, terminals and offshore facilities, and relates to the NOAA IncidentNews oil spill data catalogued here.
